title: StreamingLLM: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks
domain: AI / large language model inference / streaming KV-cache

paper_alignment.reproduced: The Figure 3 long-text language-modeling protocol is reproduced on a lower-cost member of the paper's Pythia model family: compare Window Attention (0+1024) with StreamingLLM (4+1020) over the first 20,000 tokens of PG19 using a fixed 1024-token KV cache.
paper_alignment.adaptation: Figure 3 plots Pythia-12B. This task intentionally uses Pythia-2.8B to make a first single-GPU run practical. It tests the paper's central method-level behavior but is not an exact numeric reproduction of the Pythia-12B panel.
paper_alignment.excluded: Dense attention, sliding-window re-computation, the exact Pythia-12B panel, Llama-2, Falcon, MPT, the 4M-token Figure 5 experiment, downstream tasks, latency, memory, and pre-training ablations are outside this task.

claims.statement: Under the Figure 3 protocol adapted to Pythia-2.8B, retaining four initial attention-sink tokens prevents the long-text perplexity collapse observed with a recent-token-only window after the 1024-token cache starts evicting initial tokens.
claims.experiment: Using the pinned official repository, evaluate EleutherAI/pythia-2.8b-deduped locally on the same first 20,000 PG19 test tokens in two conditions: Window Attention with start_size=0 and recent_size=1024, and StreamingLLM with start_size=4 and recent_size=1020. Enable the repository's GPT-NeoX position-shift implementation for both conditions. Save every per-token negative log-likelihood, compute 500-token binned mean NLL and perplexity, and plot both curves against token position.
claims.acceptance: Both conditions must use identical token IDs, model revision, precision, position-shift implementation, and evaluation code, and must produce all 19,999 next-token losses. Support C1 only if, over bins whose tokens are at positions 2000-20000, StreamingLLM has lower mean NLL than Window Attention in at least 80% of bins; its aggregate tail mean NLL is at least 0.5 lower; and its final 5000-token mean NLL is no more than 0.5 above its first post-eviction 500-token bin. If either run is incomplete, inputs differ, non-finite values are silently discarded, the cache is not bounded to 1024, or a different model/data source is used, the result is inconclusive. Report these adaptation-specific thresholds separately from the paper's qualitative Figure 3 claim.

requirements: Download and execute the declared immutable model revision, not a moving main branch.
Run model inference locally in FP16 on CUDA; an API model, quantized substitute, or different Pythia checkpoint cannot support the claim.
Keep controller API credentials outside the reproduced experiment and never pass them to repository or dataset code.
Record GPU, driver, CUDA, Python, PyTorch, Transformers, Datasets, NumPy, model revision, and repository commit.

environment_protocol.isolation: Create and use a task-local environment inside the run workspace when the server provides conda, micromamba, or a compatible Python 3.8 interpreter. Do not modify the controller Agent environment merely to satisfy the reproduced repository.
installation_order: Capture nvidia-smi, Python version, pip/conda package inventory, and available environment managers before changing software.
Install a server-GPU-compatible PyTorch build, then install the author-declared transformers==4.33.0 and the repository's remaining dependencies.
Run imports plus a short 32-token Pythia cache smoke test before downloading PG19 or starting the 20K-token evaluations.
Only after an evidenced baseline failure may the Agent apply a minimal compatibility patch or version deviation.
prohibited_shortcuts: Do not silently upgrade Transformers beyond 4.33.0.
Do not patch repository internals to match a newer Transformers release before attempting the author baseline.
Do not reuse packages from a prior H2O run unless their exact versions are recorded and satisfy this task's environment protocol.
required_evidence: Baseline import and cache smoke-test logs
Complete patch diff and failure log for every compatibility deviation

dataset.name: PG19 test split
dataset.source: Hugging Face Datasets pg19 loader used by the official evaluation script
dataset.selection: Tokenize the first test example with the pinned Pythia tokenizer and use input_ids[0, 0:20000]. Do not concatenate a different set of books or replace PG19 with WikiText.
dataset.integrity: Save the raw example identifier when available, raw UTF-8 text SHA256, tokenizer revision, selected input_ids SHA256, and selected token count. Use the same saved token IDs for both conditions.

metric.name: next-token negative log-likelihood and perplexity
metric.implementation: Official examples/eval_long_ppl.py semantics using unreduced cross entropy; derive perplexity as exp(mean NLL)
metric.aggregation: Preserve all per-token NLL values. Report aggregate NLL/PPL for tokens 1-1024 and 2000-20000, plus contiguous 500-token bins. Compute in float64 on CPU from saved losses and report non-finite counts without dropping them.

implementation_constraints: Preserve the official sequential one-token evaluation semantics and past_key_values flow.
The total retained KV length after eviction must be exactly 1024 in both conditions.
Apply an identical minimal GPT-NeoX/Pythia compatibility patch to both conditions when required.
Run the two conditions sequentially by default to avoid GPU-memory contention; parallel execution is allowed only after measuring that both models fit without offload, OOM, or throughput distortion.
Do not use the final aggregate PPL alone; the post-eviction curve and per-token evidence are required.
artifact_requirements: Immutable model, paper, repository, raw-text, and token-ID identifiers and hashes
Pre-install and final environment manifests plus GPU/CUDA information
Baseline smoke-test logs and any compatibility patch diff
Raw per-token NLL files for both complete 19,999-token conditions
A CSV or JSON table of 500-token bins with token range, mean NLL, perplexity, finite count, and method
A comparison JSON evaluating every acceptance condition
A regenerated NLL or log-perplexity curve with a marker at cache position 1024

budget.expected_hardware: One CUDA-capable NVIDIA GPU with at least 12 GB VRAM; 16 GB or more recommended

known_compatibility_issues: The pinned repository README requires transformers==4.33.0 but does not pin PyTorch, CUDA, Datasets, or other packages. Select compatible versions conservatively and record them.

Pythia checkpoints normally report model.config.model_type as gpt_neox, while the pinned examples/eval_long_ppl.py cache-dimension branch checks for pythia. Confirm this with the smoke test and, if reproduced, minimally change that branch to accept gpt_neox; the position-shift branch already uses gpt_neox.

Current Hugging Face Datasets releases may no longer support the paper-era pg19 loading path. Prefer a task-local compatible Datasets release or a canonical PG19 download while preserving the first-test-example selection and hashes; do not substitute WikiText.
The task uses Pythia-2.8B instead of the Pythia-12B panel shown in Figure 3. A supported result validates the lower-cost protocol adaptation, not exact numeric agreement with that panel.
Per-token evaluation is sequential and may take tens of minutes to several hours depending on the GPU. Preserve completed condition outputs so a resumed run does not recompute them.
